instruction.text: Match the generations to the historical events, which they experienced whilst growing up.

atoms.b: Cold War, 1968 student movements, Civil Rights Movement
end of the Cold War, collapse of the Soviet Union
9/11 and the war on terror, global financial crisis
global youth climate movements, migration crises, Covid-19 pandemic
Covid-19 pandemic, growing political polarisation, geopolitical tensions and global conflicts

instruction.text: Match the generations to technological advances they experienced when they grew up.

atoms.b: from b/w TV to coloured TV, first computers in companies
VHS and Walkmans, first home computers, early video games
internet at home, from mobile phones to smartphones, early social media
smartphones and social media, video and live-streaming, online gaming
tablets in childhood, smart devices, AI tools

instruction.text: Match the generations to stereotypical assumptions people make about them.

atoms.b: duty-oriented, focus on work, career and security, conservative
value independence, sometimes sceptical, want work-life-balance, cynical about activism, believe that it is pointless to try to change anything
team-oriented, look for meaning and self-realisation, politically engaged and open-minded, financially irresponsible
value diversity, climate protection and self-determination, politically aware, sometimes mistrustful or cynical about politics, radical protesters
used to fast change, awareness of mental health, materialistic, anti-social

Generations are often described with simple labels. These ideas are ((++harmful)) because they treat a whole ((++generation)) as if everyone in it were the same. In reality, people have different backgrounds, values and experiences, so it is unfair to ((++generalise)) from a few examples to millions of individuals. Such ((++stereotypes)) can influence us in the way we see others before we really know them.

This can lead to ((++prejudice)) and discrimination, especially when the labels are negative. Stereotypes can also damage a person’s sense of ((++identity)), because they feel pushed into a box that does not actually fit them. Instead of trusting easy labels, we should look at people as ((++individuals)) and base our ((++opinions)) on real contact and not on clichés about their generation.
